specificationName: Activity System Runtime Validation with Complete Log Confirmation

conflicts.description: Runtime validation uses kubectl exec (subprocess logs isolated), E2E validation uses ACP API (main process logs visible). Both target same pod but different execution contexts.
conflicts.impact: Runtime validation cannot see lifecycle logs even when they are generated, while E2E validation sees them correctly.
conflicts.resolution: Update Runtime Validation to use ACP API execution instead of kubectl exec. Change execution method: HTTP POST to ACP server → logs visible in kubectl logs.

conflicts.description: Runtime validation uses simple prompt expecting activity trigger, but activity system has thresholds that route simple tasks to direct tool calls instead of activities.
conflicts.impact: Test prompt bypasses activity system entirely, no lifecycle logs generated, validation fails even though functionality exists.
conflicts.resolution: Use complex multi-step prompts that guarantee activity triggering. Example: 'Analyze codebase, identify patterns, create documentation, commit changes'. Add direct activity invocation method.

conflicts.description: CLI behavior differs between development and container environments. Container CLI doesn't support certain flags, has different log destinations.
conflicts.impact: Validation methodologies incompatible across environments, some tests cannot run in containers.
conflicts.resolution: Document CLI differences, standardize on ACP API (environment-agnostic), add compatibility layer.

conflicts.description: Architecture separation enforces vessel flow (opencode → MCP → RPC → DB), but validation uses direct kubectl exec bypassing this pattern.
conflicts.impact: Validation doesn't test production code paths, architectural boundaries not tested for kubectl exec method.
conflicts.resolution: Align validation with production architecture (use ACP API), document kubectl exec as development tool only.

sharedComponents.conflictSummary: Different execution paths (ACP API vs kubectl exec) produce different logging observability
sharedComponents.recommendation: Refactor to ensure unified logging regardless of execution context. Add trace IDs for cross-process tracking.

sharedComponents.conflictSummary: Logs only generated when activity system triggered, simple prompts bypass entirely
sharedComponents.recommendation: Ensure memory agent logging works consistently across all invocation patterns

sharedComponents.conflictSummary: Storage logs only generated during activity execution
sharedComponents.recommendation: Add storage operation validation independent of activity system

sharedComponents.conflictSummary: Main process vs subprocess logging, different CLI behavior in container
sharedComponents.recommendation: Standardize on ACP API execution, document kubectl exec limitations

rootCauseAnalysis.details: Runtime Validation specification uses kubectl exec (development pattern) instead of ACP API (production pattern), causing logs to be isolated from kubectl logs output
rootCauseAnalysis.functionality: IMPLEMENTED - Lifecycle logging exists and works correctly
rootCauseAnalysis.validationMethod: INCORRECT - Uses wrong execution pattern to observe functionality
rootCauseAnalysis.fixComplexity: LOW - Update specification and re-run validation

actions: Update Runtime Validation specification to use ACP API
Replace simple test prompts with complex multi-step tasks
Align all validation specs to use ACP API
